requirements.requirement: Create/ensure account datauser exists on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-0a4918a071a44214 shows useradd -m -s /usr/sbin/nologin datauser followed by id confirming uid=1000(datauser). Presence reconfirmed pre- and post-restart (cmd-e755663cfbd14213, cmd-b3ad485bcee24ee3).

requirements.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB of storage under /srv/data
requirements.summary: A dedicated 512M XFS filesystem (loopback image) was mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, and xfs_quota set bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser. Reports confirm Soft=Hard=100M for datauser.

requirements.requirement: Limit enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel-level, not application-level)
requirements.summary: Functional test as datauser: 60MB write succeeded, 150MB write failed at exactly 100MB used with 'dd: error writing ... Disk quota exceeded' and nonzero exit code, directly demonstrating kernel/XFS enforcement rather than any application-layer restriction. Re-tested identically after reboot with the same result.

requirements.requirement: Limit persists across reboot (durable configuration, implied by 'enforced by the filesystem' + fstab-mounted quota)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, mount, quota config, and datauser. A native reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node became unreachable then reachable again with a new boot_id (1e0cb179... -> 973e294e...), and post-restart the /srv/data fstab mount, XFS usrquota (Enforcement: ON, 100M soft/hard), and datauser account were all shown intact, with the 150MB write test again blocked at exactly 100MB.

overall_summary: The executor created datauser, built a dedicated XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data with a 100MB usrquota for datauser, and directly demonstrated kernel-level enforcement (60MB write succeeds, 150MB write hard-blocked at exactly 100MB with EDQUOT/'Disk quota exceeded'). The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and full recovery of the mount, quota, account, and enforcement behavior post-reboot, cross-checked against the fixed before/after lifecycle boot-identity observations. All state-changing commands are traceable to the task or the mandated evidence protocol, and test artifacts were cleaned up each time.
limitations: Root's quota state was not exercised (only datauser was tested), but this is outside the stated task scope.
No prepare phase occurred (after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies solely on the executor timeline, which is complete and consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: baseline discovery (read-only), user creation, backing-file/filesystem creation, fstab entry, mount, quota configuration, and functional tests. Both the 60/150MB pre-restart test files (ok.bin/over.bin) and the post-restart test file (postreboot.bin) were explicitly cleaned up (STEP 10 in cmd-0a4918a071a44214; cleanup at end of cmd-b3ad485bcee24ee3), leaving quota usage at 0/100M. The reboot itself (cmd-7292b4544a6a4557) was required by the mandated node-restart evidence protocol. Lifecycle diff shows only expected reboot-driven artifacts (new boot_id, new systemd-private tmp dirs, listening sockets re-bound to new PIDs) with no residue attributable to the executor beyond the intended /srv/data filesystem, datauser account, and fstab entry, all of which are the task's deliverables. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
